text: 2.	On April 18, 1999, X, the greatest player in the history of Y played the final game of his career at Madison Square Garden for the team Z. He had announced his retirement just two days before this home game, not wanting a farewell tour across the league. The arena was packed. Legends of Y filled the stands: Mario Lemieux, Mark Messier, Glen Sather, Phil Esposito. A video message from Gordie Howe played on the screen. During the national anthems, Bryan Adams changed the lyrics of "O Canada" to "we're going to miss you," and the singer of "The Star-Spangled Banner" wove in the words "in the land of" followed by X’s name. The league announced that no player in the league would ever again wear his number 99. ID X (10 points), Y (3 points), and Z (7 points).
Answers: X=Wayne Gretzky, Y=ice hockey, Z=New York Rangers

3.	On April 18, 1956, X got married in a civil ceremony, with a religious ceremony following the next day at St. Nicholas Cathedral in Y. The wedding was broadcast around the world and captivated audiences across war-torn Europe. X enjoyed world-wide fame before her wedding, but she put her high-profile career in the rear window to start a more “serene” life with her new husband. After her tragic death, the United States and Y both issued postage stamps featuring the same portait, but with different names on the stamp because of a US law forbidding the depiction of foreign heads of states on its postage stamps. ID X (10 points) and Y (5 points).

4.	At 5:12 AM on April 18, 1906, residents of X were jolted awake by a massive earthquake estimated at 7.9 on the Richter scale. The earthquake itself caused enormous damage, but the fires that followed were far worse — they burned for three days and destroyed over 80% of the city. More than 3,000 people perished, making it one of the deadliest natural disasters in the country’s history. Over half the city's population of 400,000 was left homeless. The earthquake damaged the office of Amadeo Giannini’s tiny Bank of Italy, but he was able to get to the gold and silver in his vault. In the chaos following the earthquake, Giannini setup a makeshift bank on a wharf in the city’s Italian neighborhood and started making loans to desperate residents “on a handshake.” In 1930 he changed the name of his bank to Y. By the time Giannini died in 1949, Y was the largest bank in the world. ID X (10 points) and Y (10 points). ‎<attached: 00120591-PHOTO-2026-04-18-08-12-32.jpg>
